classification.difficultyReason: Compare two compound depreciation rates through total percentage reductions and fleet values after six years.

content.prompt: Taxis depreciate at $50\%$ p.a., and other cars depreciate at $22.5\%$ p.a.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the total percentage reduction in value on each type of vehicle after six years? Give percentages correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The annual value multipliers are $1-0.50=0.50$ for taxis and $1-0.225=0.775$ for other cars.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxi percentage reduction}&=(1-0.50^6)\times100\%\\\text{Taxi percentage reduction}&=98.4375\%\\\text{Taxi percentage reduction}&\approx98.4\%\\\text{Other-car percentage reduction}&=(1-0.775^6)\times100\%\\\text{Other-car percentage reduction}&\approx78.3\%.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the difference in value after six years of a fleet of taxis and a fleet of other cars, if both fleets originally cost $\$10\,000\,000$? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.short: The fleet of other cars is worth $\$2\,010\,507.03$ more.
answer.worked:
Using $A_n=P(1-R)^n$:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxi fleet value}&=10\,000\,000(1-0.50)^6\\\text{Taxi fleet value}&=\$156\,250\\\text{Other-car fleet value}&=10\,000\,000(1-0.225)^6\\\text{Other-car fleet value}&\approx\$2\,166\,757.03\\\text{Difference}&=10\,000\,000(0.775^6-0.50^6)\\\text{Difference}&\approx\$2\,010\,507.03.\end{align*}$$

The fleet of other cars is worth more.
